tool_args.old_string: \paragraph{Why does generation degrade at repo level?} Output space complexity increases nonlinearly: function-level outputs are short status strings (e.g., ``PASS'' or brief error messages, mean ${\sim}$5--15 tokens); repo-level outputs are unconstrained execution traces (mean ${\sim}$477 tokens) where errors compound multiplicatively, causing format collapse (53--74\% unparseable). Even parseable outputs achieve only 38--43\% accuracy, below majority baseline; forced parsing rescues 90.6\% of unparseable outputs but achieves only 49.4\% accuracy, confirming the bottleneck is semantic (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(c)). Four targeted interventions---increased LoRA capacity (rank~32), majority voting ($K{=}3$), relaxed output matching, and model scaling (4B$\to$8B)---all fail to close the gap (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(g)). Checkpoint selection does not explain the gap: matched epoch-3 comparisons yield gaps of 20--23\pp{} (comparable to val-selected gaps), and \cls{} checkpoint ablation shows $<$1\pp{} variation across epochs, with the val-selected checkpoint performing no better than the worst epoch (Appendix~\ref{app:cwm_convergence}). This extends formulation-dependent tradeoffs~\cite{raffel2020t5} to a regime where output complexity makes format compliance a dominant failure mode. \cwm{} eval loss reaches its minimum within 5\% of training and increases monotonically across all seeds; a DeepSeek epoch-1 checkpoint achieves 75.45\% vs.\ 57.31\% at epoch~3, reducing the gap to ${\sim}$9\pp{} but retaining 66.4\% unparseable (Appendix~\ref{app:cwm_convergence}).

\paragraph{Repair, Mutation Testing, and Task Framing.}
CodeRL~\cite{le2022coderl}, AlphaCode~\cite{li2022alphacode,alphacode2023team}, and Reflexion~\cite{shinn2023reflexion} use execution feedback for repair. SWE-bench~\cite{jimenez2024swebench,chowdhury2024swebenchverified} provides benchmarks; SWE-agent~\cite{yang2024sweagent} and Agentless~\cite{xia2024agentless} demonstrate pipelines where verification is a bottleneck~\cite{yang2025aprsurvey}. Predictive mutation testing~\cite{tufano2019predictive,kim2022predictive,wang2024llmmutation,jain2023contextual} shares our per-test structure. LoRA~\cite{hu2022lora} and QLoRA~\cite{dettmers2024qlora} enable parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Task framing---how a problem is cast as a model's input--output mapping---systematically affects performance: \citet{raffel2020t5} showed that classification, generation, and span-extraction formulations yield different accuracy--efficiency tradeoffs across NLP tasks. We apply this paradigm to code verification, holding architecture and training data constant while varying only the formulation; our finding that complexity moderates the classification--generation tradeoff extends their analysis to a new domain.
